newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes firm in late Asia after API data.
newsitem.headline: Crudes firm in late Asia after API data.

text.p: Crude oil prices were firm in late Asian trading on Wednesday following the release overnight of the weekly API data on crude oil and product stocks, traders said.

The latest API data showed that U.S. crude oil stocks held in primary storage fell 3.50 million barrels in the week ended November 15 to 302.31 million barrels. Distillate stocks increased by 920,000 barrels, while heating oil stocks shrank 854,000 barrels in the week ending November 15.
In late trading, January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $23.40/23.50.
On SIMEX, January Brent was indicated at $23.41/23.49 at 0905 GMT.
In spreads, Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed a touch wider on the back of Brent's strength. January was notionally assessed at $1.95/2.00, against late U.S. trading levels of $1.85/1.95.

In the wet market, a January Oman was believed traded between a major and a Japanese trading firm at MPM plus 12 cents. The level was higher than an earlier deal for a January cargo believed done at MPM plus 10 cents between a trader and a major. A January Qatar Marine was also reported traded.
The deal, said done between a major and a Japanese oil company, is believed to have been at QGPC plus 45 cents, a few cents below a deal believed done last week.

Dubai premiums appeared well-supported, with a deal widely believed done at around dated Brent plus 75 to 80 cents. The deal, believed to have been done between a trader and a Japanese oil refining company, appears to be a date-guaranteed cargo with additional premiums paid for the guarantee.
Trading in regional crudes appeared light, with Minas assessed fetching a premium of about 40 cents above the official selling price.--M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo (+813 5473 3706)
